paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. David says it himself: "it is not by sword or spear that the LORD saves; for the battle is the LORD's" (1 Samuel 17:47). Everybody in that valley was sizing up bronze and spears, and David was looking at WHO the battle belongs to. Goliath's size was real, and the fear was real. But the size of the problem was never the thing that decided it.

Look at what David leans on when Saul says he's just a boy. He doesn't point to himself. He says, "The LORD, who delivered me from the claws of the lion and the bear, will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine" (1 Samuel 17:37). I think David's past was more than a pile of old stories to him. It was proof of who had been with him all along. And when Saul's armor didn't fit, David took it off and walked out with what he knew (1 Samuel 17:39-40).

So here's what I'd carry out of my bakery today, baker. Your Goliath might be a bill, a hard talk or a morning that keeps showing up, and you can't out-armor it. But you can remember who has already brought you through, and walk toward it knowing the battle is the LORD's. This story isn't over, either, because David's walk is only getting started.
